title: In the loop
brief: Volts are measured across a part. Amps are measured through it: the current has to flow through the meter.
The circuit's already built and lit. Pull the wire that closes the loop (Remove tool), switch the meter to A, and bridge the gap with the probes: red on the LED's side, black on the − rail.
Careful: in A mode the meter is nearly a short (0.1 Ω). Across a part it steals the current; across the supply it blows its 200 mA fuse. The supply's limit is 1 A this time.
lesson: A voltmeter goes across a part and barely disturbs anything. An ammeter goes in series and becomes part of the loop. Same meter, opposite rules, which is why real meters have a separate socket for amps.
